Exercising the forecasting workflow

Source: vignettes/zero-shot-workflow.Rmd
zero-shot-workflow.Rmd

This vignette exercises the engine and adapter surfaces with stub, a weight-free random-walk fixture. It is not a foundation model — it exists so the engine and its adapters can be demonstrated and tested without a download. Every output below is produced when this vignette is built.

For the same workflow driven by a real checkpoint, see vignette("timesfm-zero-shot").

Load a model

zuk_pretrained() returns a uniform model handle. The stub branch is entirely local and deterministic:

library(zukzeit)

model <- zuk_pretrained("stub")

Before doing any work, ask what the model can do. The capability report is checked before inference, so an unsupported request fails fast with a clear message instead of deep inside a tensor op:

zuk_capabilities(model)
#> <zuk_capabilities>
#>   architecture:      stub
#>   max_context:       512        max_horizon: Inf
#>   quantiles:         native        levels: arbitrary
#>   multivariate:      FALSE        samples:   FALSE
#>   past_covariates:   FALSE        future_covariates: FALSE
#>   static_covariates: FALSE        fine_tunable: FALSE
#>   license:           MIT

Requests are validated against that report at the engine boundary, not after it:

forecast(model, data.frame(t = 1:10, y = as.numeric(1:10)),
         h = 5, index = "t", target = "y", quantile_levels = c(0.1, 1.5))
#> Error in `zuk_infer()`:
#> ! Quantile levels must be unique finite probabilities strictly between 0
#>   and 1.

A panel to forecast

Two monthly series, split into observed history and the twelve months held back to score against:

set.seed(1)
months <- seq(as.Date("2015-01-01"), by = "month", length.out = 96)
panel <- data.frame(
  store = rep(c("north", "south"), each = length(months)),
  month = rep(months, 2),
  sales = c(
    100 + 0.8 * seq_along(months) + 10 * sin(seq_along(months) * pi / 6),
    50 + 0.3 * seq_along(months) + 4 * cos(seq_along(months) * pi / 6)
  ) + rnorm(2 * length(months), sd = 2)
)

split_at <- max(months) - 365
history <- panel[panel$month <= split_at, ]
actuals <- panel[panel$month > split_at, ]
nrow(history)
#> [1] 168
nrow(actuals)
#> [1] 24

Path 1 — the forecast() convenience surface

Hand a panel of history and a horizon; get a forecast object back. This path has no optional dependencies at all — a plain data frame is enough, as long as the index and target columns are named:

fc <- forecast(model, history, h = 12,
               index = "month", key = "store", target = "sales",
               quantile_levels = c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9))

fc
#> <zuk_forecast> of "sales"
#> 2 series x horizon, quantile levels 0.1, 0.5, and 0.9
#>    store      month    .mean .distribution
#> 1  north 2022-01-01 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 2  north 2022-02-01 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 3  north 2022-03-04 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 4  north 2022-04-04 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 5  north 2022-05-05 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 6  north 2022-06-05 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 7  north 2022-07-06 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 8  north 2022-08-06 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 9  north 2022-09-06 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 10 north 2022-10-07 164.1529   quantile[3]

The forecast carries both views of the same predicted quantiles: a distributional column for the tidyverts, and the raw quantile matrix for the tidymodels prediction columns.

head(as.data.frame(fc), 3)
#>   store      month    .mean .distribution
#> 1 north 2022-01-01 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 2 north 2022-02-01 164.1529   quantile[3]
#> 3 north 2022-03-04 164.1529   quantile[3]

Note that the future index comes back as Date, the type it went in as. The engine extends an index in its own units, so a yearmonth panel returns yearmonth, an hourly POSIXct panel returns POSIXct, and the result joins straight back onto the data it came from.

Path 2 — the tidyverts

zukzeit registers a method on fabletools::as_fable() rather than exporting a generic of its own, so the verb keeps working when fabletools and zukzeit are both attached. Call it qualified, or library(fabletools) first.

# yearmonth is the natural index for monthly data: calendar months are not
# equally spaced in days, so a Date index would put the forecasts a few days
# off the observed month starts and nothing would join.
as_monthly <- function(data) {
  data$month <- tsibble::yearmonth(data$month)
  tsibble::as_tsibble(data, index = month, key = store)
}
history_tsbl <- as_monthly(history)
actuals_tsbl <- as_monthly(actuals)

fabletools::as_fable(forecast(model, history_tsbl, h = 12)) |>
  fabletools::accuracy(actuals_tsbl)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   store .type    ME  RMSE   MAE   MPE  MAPE  MASE RMSSE  ACF1
#>   <chr> <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 north Test   9.41 10.7   9.41  5.34  5.34   NaN   NaN 0.725
#> 2 south Test  -4.73  5.83  5.06 -6.35  6.75   NaN   NaN 0.458

TSFM() is the other tidyverts route: it composes inside fabletools::model() next to any other model definition, one key at a time.

fits <- fabletools::model(history_tsbl, zukzeit = TSFM(sales, model_id = "stub"))
fits
#> # A mable: 2 x 2
#> # Key:     store [2]
#>   store      zukzeit
#>   <chr>      <model>
#> 1 north <TSFM[stub]>
#> 2 south <TSFM[stub]>

fabletools::forecast(fits, h = 3)
#> # A fable: 6 x 5 [1M]
#> # Key:     store, .model [2]
#>   store .model     month       sales .mean
#>   <chr> <chr>      <mth>      <dist> <dbl>
#> 1 north zukzeit 2022 Jan quantile[3] 164. 
#> 2 north zukzeit 2022 Feb quantile[3] 164. 
#> 3 north zukzeit 2022 Mar quantile[3] 164. 
#> 4 south zukzeit 2022 Jan quantile[3]  81.6
#> 5 south zukzeit 2022 Feb quantile[3]  81.6
#> 6 south zukzeit 2022 Mar quantile[3]  81.6

Path 3 — a tidymodels workflow

The tidymodels surface is a parsnip spec inside a workflow(). The model is chosen by the engine’s model_id; everything else stays the same.

library(parsnip)
library(workflows)

spec <- zuk_reg(context_length = 512L) |>
  set_engine("zukzeit",
             model_id = "stub",
             index    = "month",
             id       = "store")

wf <- workflow() |>
  add_variables(outcomes = sales, predictors = c(month, store)) |>
  add_model(spec)

fitted <- fit(wf, data = history)
head(predict(fitted, new_data = actuals[, c("store", "month")]), 3)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   .pred
#>   <dbl>
#> 1  164.
#> 2  164.
#> 3  164.

add_variables() rather than add_formula() is deliberate. index and id name columns the engine reads out of the data it is handed, and a formula preprocessor keeps only the terms in the formula — which would drop store before the engine ever sees it.

Tuning the context length

context_length is a tunable dials parameter, so a rolling-origin search over rsample resamples works out of the box:

library(tune)
library(rsample)

tuned <- tune_grid(
  workflow() |>
    add_variables(outcomes = sales, predictors = c(month, store)) |>
    add_model(zuk_reg(context_length = tune()) |>
                set_engine("zukzeit", model_id = "stub",
                           index = "month", id = "store")),
  resamples = sliding_period(history[history$store == "north", ],
                             index = month, period = "year",
                             lookback = Inf, assess_stop = 1),
  grid = dials::grid_regular(context_length(range = c(12L, 48L)), levels = 3)
)

show_best(tuned, metric = "rmse")
#> # A tibble: 3 × 7
#>   context_length .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config        
#>            <int> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>          
#> 1             12 rmse    standard    8.00     6   0.560 pre0_mod1_post0
#> 2             30 rmse    standard    8.00     6   0.560 pre0_mod2_post0
#> 3             48 rmse    standard    8.00     6   0.560 pre0_mod3_post0

Every candidate scores the same here, and that is the expected answer: the stub forecasts the last observed value, so how much history it keeps cannot change its point forecast. Run the same search against TimesFM for a result that means something — vignette("rolling-origin-tuning") walks it in more detail.

Clean up

The constructed handle is held in a bounded in-session cache. Evicting it does not touch anything on disk:

zuk_cache_status()
#>                                model_id
#> 1       google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch
#> 2                      amazon/chronos-2
#> 3                   Datadog/Toto-2.0-4m
#> 4 ibm-granite/granite-timeseries-ttm-r2
#> 5                                  stub
#>                                   revision device disk_cached resident
#> 1 1d952420fba87f3c6dee4f240de0f1a0fbc790e3   <NA>       FALSE    FALSE

#> 3 8306a9801cf98c0f5ffe4b2dcc8f496e616d84d9   <NA>       FALSE    FALSE

zuk_unload("stub")

Status

The public workflow above is real, but its model is deliberately only a test fixture. TimesFM 2.5 is the first implemented release model; see vignette("timesfm-zero-shot") for the same surfaces driven by real weights. TTM remains a registered scaffold, and Chronos-2 is rejected before any network or tensor work until its native port lands.
